C6.1.q: How is warp different from a filter?
options: Warp removes harmonics; a filter can only add them
Warp changes the note; a filter changes the loudness
Warp can add harmonics; a filter can only take them away
Warp needs a second oscillator; a filter does not
C6.1.why: Warp changes the wave's outline, so it can add harmonics, while a filter can only take them away.

C6.1.q: Why does the note stay the same when you turn warp up?
options: The wave still repeats just as often
The filter holds the pitch in place
Hold is switched on for the note
The new harmonics are too quiet to hear
C6.1.why: Pitch comes from how often the wave repeats, and warp does not change that.

C6.1.q: You set a saw to Mirror at 100%. What happens to the sound?
options: It turns brighter and buzzier, like a pulse
It jumps up to a higher note
It becomes a pure tone with one harmonic
It turns soft and hollow, like a triangle
C6.1.why: Read forwards then backwards, the saw's outline becomes a triangle, and a new outline means different harmonics.

C6.2.q: Why does the pitch hold when sync reads the wave faster?
options: The wave is read forwards and then backwards
The wave starts again at the end of every cycle
A macro keeps pulling the pitch back down
The extra copies are too quiet to hear
C6.2.why: Sync restarts the wave every time the cycle ends, so the cycle is as long as before.

C6.2.q: What makes sync sound torn and bright?
options: A filter opens wider as the amount is turned up
A second oscillator plays slightly out of tune with the first
The wave gets louder until its top is cut flat
The last copy of the wave is cut short, leaving a sharp edge
C6.2.why: The cut-short copy leaves a sharp edge, and sharp edges are bright.

C6.2.q: You want to play the sync sweep from one knob you can name. What do you do?
options: Send a macro to Warp amount and turn the macro
Leave Warp amount at full and play other notes
Change the shape from saw to sine and back
Switch Hold off and strike the key harder
C6.2.why: The sweep of the amount is the sound, so a macro sent to Warp amount lets you play it.

C6.3.q: What does Squeeze do to a square wave?
options: Makes it repeat faster, raising the pitch
Rounds off its corners, turning it into a sine
Makes the high part shorter, turning it into a pulse
Reads it forwards and then backwards
C6.3.why: Squeeze hurries through the first half, so the square's high part gets shorter and its pulse width changes.

C6.3.q: How does a narrow pulse sound next to a square, and why?
options: Hollower, because the even harmonics are taken out
Thinner and more nasal, because even harmonics come in
Duller, because the high harmonics are filtered off
Lower, because the wave repeats less often
C6.3.why: A square has only odd harmonics, and narrowing the pulse lets the even ones in, which sounds thinner and more nasal.

C6.3.q: What do you get by moving the pulse width slowly back and forth?
options: A steady rise and fall in the note's pitch
A tone that fades slowly away to silence
A clean jump up an octave and back
A rich, shifting tone, as in string and pad patches
C6.3.why: Slowly moving the pulse width gives a rich, animated tone.

C6.4.q: What happens when a pitch wobble is sped up until it is as fast as a note?
options: You stop hearing the pitch move and hear new harmonics
The vibrato gets wider and easier to hear
The note gets louder but keeps its tone
The note drops out and leaves a gap
C6.4.why: FM is pitch modulation so fast that it is heard as tone, not as movement.

C6.4.q: With FM on, B sits an octave and 6 semitones above A. Why does it clang?
options: The FM amount has been turned up too far
Oscillator B is now loud enough to be heard
The new partials no longer line up with the note's harmonics
The envelope is making the note far too short
C6.4.why: B's pitch against A's sets where the new partials fall, and in between whole octaves they miss the harmonics.

C6.4.q: How do you make a bell that starts bright and mellows as it rings out?
options: Send a slow LFO to oscillator A's pitch
Send an envelope to the FM amount
Turn the FM amount up and leave it
Switch oscillator B on and raise its level
C6.4.why: An envelope on the FM amount gives a bright strike that mellows to a pure tone.

C6.5.q: Two pure tones are ring modulated at full amount. What comes out?
options: Both original tones, a little louder
The original tones plus two new ones
Only the lower tone, an octave down
Only their sum and their difference
C6.5.why: Two pure tones give one tone at the sum of their frequencies and one at the difference, and the originals are gone.

C6.5.q: How does ring modulation combine oscillators A and B?
options: It multiplies one signal by the other
It adds one signal to the other
It plays one signal after the other
It uses one signal to filter the other
C6.5.why: Ring modulation multiplies one signal by another.

C6.5.q: With two sines, how does FM differ from ring modulation as you turn it up?
options: Ring keeps adding pairs of partials; FM makes just one pair
FM changes the note's loudness; ring changes its pitch
FM keeps adding pairs of partials; ring makes just one pair
Ring needs B to be heard; FM works with B off
C6.5.why: FM makes many pairs of partials as it rises, while ring modulation makes one pair per pair of harmonics.

C6.C.q: The hidden sound no longer contains the note being played. What should you suspect?
options: Sync
Ring modulation
Bend
Squeeze
C6.C.why: Ring modulation removes the played note and leaves new tones in its place.

C6.C.q: The hidden sound's added brightness is smooth, not torn. Which should you try?
options: Sync or bend
Sync or squeeze
Bend or squeeze
Sync only
C6.C.why: A smooth brightness points to bend or squeeze, while a torn, vowel-like one is sync.

C6.C.q: In an FM round, the new partials are further apart than yours. What do you change?
options: The pitch of oscillator B
The level of oscillator B
The FM amount
The warp amount
C6.C.why: With FM, B's pitch sets how far apart the new partials are.

C7.1.q: Why does distortion make a sound brighter?
options: It turns up the high harmonics that were already there
It takes away the low harmonics below a set point
It reshapes the wave, and a new shape means new harmonics
It plays a second, higher note on top
C7.1.why: Distortion reshapes a signal that is too big to fit, and the changed shape has new harmonics.

C7.1.q: On the scope the smooth wave has become a staircase. Which type is on?
options: Soft clip
Crush
Hard clip
Fold
C7.1.why: Crush rounds every value to a coarse grid of steps, which looks like a staircase.

C7.1.q: You want the weight of the clean sound with some distorted edge. What do you do?
options: Turn Drive all the way up
Turn Drive all the way down
Turn Mix all the way up
Turn Mix down to about half
C7.1.why: Mix blends the clean sound back in with the distorted one.

C7.2.q: Cutting High on the EQ made the sound duller but not muffled. Why?
options: The high harmonics are quieter, not gone
The low harmonics were boosted to match
The EQ only works on the middle band
The high harmonics were removed past a point
C7.2.why: An EQ turns a region down by a set amount, while a filter removes everything past a point.

C7.2.q: A sound is too thin and needs more weight at the bottom. What do you do?
options: Cut the low band
Boost the high band
Boost the low band
Cut the middle band
C7.2.why: The low band turns the bottom end up or down, and boosting it makes the sound heavier.

C7.2.q: What is the usual way to find and fix a boxy part of a sound?
options: Cut Low and High until only the boxy part is left
Boost Mid, sweep its frequency to find it, then cut
Cut Mid fully, then sweep until the sound goes quiet
Boost all three bands, then turn the level down
C7.2.why: A big boost swept across the range makes the problem jump out, and then you set the amount you want.

C7.3.q: The threshold is set so high that no note reaches it. What does the compressor do?
options: It turns every note down equally
It turns down only the soft notes
It turns down only the start of each note
Nothing: no note is turned down
C7.3.why: A compressor only turns down what goes over the threshold.

C7.3.q: After compressing, you turn Make-up up. What happens to the soft notes?
options: They end up much louder than before
They stay as quiet as before
They are turned down more than hard notes
They get a sharper front than hard notes
C7.3.why: Make-up gain brings the level back up, which lifts the quiet parts.

C7.3.q: Which setting lets the very start of a hard note through at full level?
options: A fast attack
A fast release
A slow attack
A higher ratio
C7.3.why: With a slow attack the start gets through before the compressor catches up.

C7.4.q: Why do a chorus's copies drift flat and sharp against the original?
options: Each copy comes from an extra detuned oscillator
Their delays keep changing, which shifts the pitch slightly
Each copy is passed through a moving filter
Their levels keep changing, which sounds like pitch
C7.4.why: A chorus keeps changing each copy's delay, and a changing delay raises or lowers the pitch a little.

C7.4.q: With Depth at 0, what does the chorus sound like?
options: A gentle swirl that moves slowly
A fast wobble that sounds out of tune
No effect: only the original sound
A hollow, static colour with no movement
C7.4.why: Depth is how far the copies drift, so at 0 they sit still and give a fixed, hollow colour.

C7.4.q: How is chorus different from unison?
options: Chorus is applied afterwards to the whole sound; unison is inside each note
Chorus is inside each note; unison is applied afterwards to the whole sound
Chorus changes only the pitch; unison changes only the loudness of each note
Chorus adds echoes after each note; unison adds a long smooth wash
C7.4.why: Unison is extra oscillators inside each note, and chorus is applied afterwards to everything at once.

C7.5.q: You want exactly one echo after each note. What do you set?
options: Feedback to about 75%
Time to half a beat
Feedback to 0
Time to about 60 ms
C7.5.why: Feedback sets how many echoes there are, and with none there is a single echo.

C7.5.q: What happens when the delay time is made very short?
options: The echoes blur into a metallic flutter stuck to the note
The echoes stop and the note is left clean
The echoes get louder with every repeat
The echoes land exactly on every click
C7.5.why: Very short times stop sounding like separate echoes and colour the tone.

C7.5.q: Why set the delay time in beats?
options: The echoes die away more slowly
The echoes keep one fixed gap at any tempo
The delay makes more echoes for each note
The echoes stay in time when the tempo changes
C7.5.why: Set in beats, the delay time follows the tempo, so the echoes stay on the rhythm.

options: A few clear echoes spaced evenly in time
Thousands of echoes too close together to hear separately
Copies of the sound drifting slightly out of tune
One long echo that repeats on the beat
C7.6.why: Reverb is a dense wash of echoes from every surface, which then dies away.

C7.6.q: You want the sound to seem further away without making the tail longer. What do you do?
options: Turn Mix down
Turn Mix up
Turn Size up
Turn Size down
C7.6.why: Mix sets how far away the sound seems, and Size sets how long the tail lasts.

C7.6.q: Which kind of playing suits a long reverb best?
options: A fast run of short notes
Quick repeated notes with no gaps
Fast playing with Mix at full
Single notes with long gaps after them
C7.6.why: Long tails blur fast notes together, while a single note has room to ring.

C7.C.q: The hidden sound differs in the tone itself, not in what follows the note. Which effects do you check?
options: Delay or reverb
Distortion or EQ
Delay or EQ
Reverb or distortion
C7.C.why: A change in the tone itself points to distortion or EQ.

C7.C.q: After the note you hear separate repeats, not a smooth wash. Which effect is it?
options: A reverb
A distortion
An EQ
A delay
C7.C.why: Separate repeats are a delay, and a smooth wash is a reverb.

C7.C.q: How can you judge the hidden sound's delay time by ear?
options: Count how many echoes there are
Listen to how bright the echoes are
Count the gap between the echoes
Listen to how long the space rings
C7.C.why: The gap between echoes is the delay time, so counting it tells you the setting.
